title: Works Well as Simple Dehydrator; Slower, Less Versatile Than More Expensive Competing Product
text:
Works Well as Simple Dehydrator; Slower, Less Versatile Than More Expensive Competing Product. [[VIDEOID:moTYGPGLRDB4O4]]This bargain-priced (about $24) OSTER FPSTDH0101 ELECTRIC FOOD DEHYDRATOR works well as a dehydrator, but the more expensive (about $60) [[ASIN:B0090WOCN0 Nesco FD-75A 700-Watt Food Dehydrator]] works faster, is easier to clean, has adjustable temperature settings, and accommodates more trays. See the accompanying video slide show for my side-by-side comparison of these two dehydrators. (I purchased the Nesco Pro model from Amazon, and received the Oster model through Amazon Vine.)

SIGNIFICANT DIFFERENCES: The Oster and Nesco models have two very significant differences. First, the Oster electrical drying unit is bottom-mounted, while the Nesco electrical drying unit is top-mounted. The bottom-mounted drying unit is a real disadvantage, because fruit, vegetable, and meat juices invariably drip into the base from the drying trays above. Since the electrical base cannot be immersed in water, the base must always be cleaned carefully by hand. This isn't difficult, but it's much harder to remove juices from the base than from the trays. In contrast, the top-mounted Nesco drying unit stays clean throughout the drying process. At most, it requires a quick wipe with a moist cloth or paper towel. The bottom tray of the Nesco model is even easier to clean than the trays.

Second, the Oster drying unit is equipped with an on/off switch, while the Nesco drying unit is equipped with an adjustable temperature-setting dial. In this respect, the Nesco model is far superior to the Oster model, because the Oster model with the simple on/of switch has only one drying temperature. With the Nesco model, you can start your food drying at a higher temperature, and dial it down after a few hours to the "normal" 135-140 degrees, to speed up the drying times. You can also adjust the temperature from 95 degrees to 160 degrees, to accommodate foods needing lower (e.g., herbs) or higher (e.g., jerky) temperatures to dry optimally. A disadvantage of the Nesco model is that it lacks an on/off switch, and can only be stopped by unplugging the whole unit.

SIZE AND CAPACITY: The Oster and Nesco dehydrators are almost exactly the same size, and take up the same amount of countertop space. However, the Oster has only four (4) trays, and doesn't appear to be expandable. (The instruction booklet makes no mention of the availability of expansion trays.) My photos show the Nesco model with 4 trays, but the basic Nesco Pro model has five (5) trays, and is expandable to 12-14 trays.

With only 4 trays, the Oster dehydrator's capacity is limited to the equivalent of what you see in the photos: 1/2 cup blueberries, 1/2 apple, 1 pear, 2 extra-large bell peppers (1/2 pepper in green, red, orange, yellow). With the Nesco model, you can dry more food at one time, by using more trays (and maybe use a bit less electricity). With 9 trays, the Nesco model will dry 9 extra-large peaches.

TRAYS: The Oster and Nesco trays are also nearly identical in size. The Oster trays are made of a flexible plastic-netting material, the Nesco trays are made of a hard plastic more like Bakelite. The Oster trays are dishwasher-safe; the Nesco trays can be washed in the dishwasher if you remove them before the start of the drying cycle.

However, the trays for both the Oster and Nesco models are quite easy to clean without even using a dishwasher. Just soak the trays for a couple of minutes in hot, soapy water; then use a soft dish brush to remove any sticky bits. Because of the differing "hole patterns", the Oster trays pick up a few more bits than the Nesco trays, but the difference is negligible. All the trays fit in a large kitchen sink.

FOOD PREPARATION: Fruits and vegetables should be cored and seeded, and cut into 1/4-inch slices. Food with edible skins (apples, pears) can be peeled or not. Fruits that turn brown if left exposed to the air can be tossed with orange juice, pineapple juice, or a product like Fruit Fresh to prevent this during drying. (I used Fruit Fresh in my test.) The easiest way to slice the food for drying is to put it through a food processor, using the widest possible slicing blade. This goes very quickly, and gives you uniform slices that will dry uniformly. The food processor cleanup is easy.

DRYING TIME: In my test, I halved a cup of blueberries (blanched first in boiling water), an apple, two pears, and four different-colored bell peppers; then I arranged them in similar tray patterns and stacked the trays in the same order. After 4-1/2 hours at 138 degrees, the Nesco model had dried everything except the blueberries to flexible-leather consistency; after 6 hours, the Oster model (at an unknown temperature) had accomplished the same thing.

The instruction booklet for the Oster model suggested 12-18 hours for the fruits and 14-18 hours for bell peppers; the instruction booklet for the Nesco model suggested 4-10 hours for apples, 6-16 hours for pears, and 5-12 hours for bell peppers. Obviously, both the Oster and Nesco units dried the food in less time. In my experience, foods usually dry in less time, so I always check back after 3 hours.

With both the Oster and Nesco models, you will need to remove some food or rearrange it on the trays, or rearrange the food trays themselves, before the full drying time is up. Even the most uniformly-sliced food will dry at slightly different rates because of air circulation patterns inside the stacks of trays.

After 9 hours, both the Oster and Nesco models were still working on the blueberries. Perhaps I didn't blanch the berries properly to break the skins. Some of the berries had dried and achieved raisin-like status, but most had a lot of liquid left inside. I decided it wasn't worth the cost of electricity to continue drying the blueberries, and abandoned the test there. If anything, the Oster was ahead of the Nesco after 9 hours.

CONCLUSION: If you're serious about drying food--making trail mix, preserving summer's bounty, drying herbs, making jerky, or stocking an emergency pantry--you will want a full-featured dehydrator like the Nesco Pro model. The Nesco Pro comes with 5 trays, and with clean-a-screen and fruit roll sheets (2 of each). These sheets are used, respectively, for drying herbs (to prevent the dried bits from falling through the holes in the trays) and for drying fruit purees. Nesco also sells a "jerky gun" as an extra food dehydrator accessory for making uniform strips of jerky from ground meat. (The jerky gun can be used with any food dehydrator.)

If you're not so sure about your commitment to drying food, then you may want to start with this 4-tray Oster model; or with Nesco's bargain-priced (about $31) 4-tray [[ASIN:B003I4F7AS Nesco American Harvest FD-37 400 Watt Food Dehydrator]], which has a top-mounted drying fan, is expandable to 7 trays, and can use the Nesco clean-a-screen and fruit roll sheets. Because of the single temperature setting and the bottom-mounted drying unit, I rate this OSTER 4-TRAY ELECTRICAL FOOD DEHYDRATOR at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).

product_metadata.title: Oster FPSTDH0101 4-Tray Electric Food Dehydrator, White
features: Countertop food dehydrator dries food in hours instead of days
Simple one-touch operation; centrally located heater for efficient results
Electric fan circulates air for faster, more even drying with no tray rotation necessary
4 adjustable and removable trays included; dishwasher-safe lid and trays
description: Fun and easy to use, this countertop food dehydrator makes all-natural beef or turkey jerky, homemade trail mix, apple snacks, banana chips, dried soup mixes, dried herbs and spices, and more in a matter of hours instead of days--it can also be used to make potpourri and dried flowers for any occasion. Simply lay the food out flat on the trays, secure the lid in place, press the toggle switch to "on", and it takes care of the rest. The unit's centrally located heater dries foods quickly and efficiently, while its electric fan circulates air for faster, more even drying with no tray rotation necessary. Four adjustable and removable trays come included. When finished, the lid and trays clean up easily by hand or in the dishwasher. The food dehydrator measures 14 by 13 by 9 inches.
